title: Structure à l'infini des Mg,ν [pages 1 à 90, dont table des matières] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting: the boundary stratification of the Deligne–Mumford compactification \bar M_{g,ν} by stable dual graphs G (the 'MD-graphes'). M_G is the stratum of curves with dual graph G. ΠM_G is its fundamental groupoid, and Γ_G = Aut G acts on it. A(G) is the set of edges, i.e. nodes. On the previous page, S_AΠM_G := ΠM*_{G,G'} is the fundamental groupoid of a deleted (punctured) tubular neighbourhood of M_G, taken in the open part. Topologically this is the complement of the coordinate hyperplanes in the normal bundle ⊕_{e∈A} L_e, so it is a (C*)^A-bundle up to the twist by automorphisms. Hence it is an extension of ΠM_G by the local system Z^{A(G)}, twisted by the action of Γ' ⊂ Γ_G on A(G). Its generators are the Dehn twists around the vanishing cycles.

This page: let C ⊂ A(G) be Γ'-stable. The projection of local systems Z^{A(G)} → Z^C lets one push out the extension. This gives a quotient extension (S_CΠM_G, Γ') of (ΠM_G, Γ') by Z^C (eq. 117). Geometrically one kills the twists around the nodes not in C. The result is the groupoid of the punctured neighbourhood of M_G inside the closure of the stratum M_{G/C}, smoothing only the nodes in C.

A crossed-out passage identifies this, for Γ' = Γ^!_{G,G/C}, with ΠM*_{G,G/C}. Grothendieck prefers instead to make the data explicit via generalization morphisms. Let G' ≅ G/C be the contraction of the edges in C, with A' = A \ C. Then there is a canonical map S_AΠM_G → S_{A'}ΠM_{G'} (eq. 118, the second of two equations numbered 118). It comes from the inclusion of the deleted neighbourhood of M_G into that of M_{G'}, modulo base-change paths.

This map fits into a commutative square (eq. 119):
- the left vertical arrow S_A → S_C kills Z^{A'};
- the right vertical arrow S_{A'}ΠM_{G'} → ΠM_{G'} also kills Z^{A'};
- the bottom row is S_CΠM_G → ΠM_{G'}.

The square is equivariant for Γ_{G,G'}, the stabilizer of C. The next page factors the bottom row through Γ^!_{G,G'} (eqs. 121–122). It then states that transitivity (eq. 105) amounts to the functoriality of G ↦ S_AΠM_G on the category of MD-graphs with generalization (contraction) morphisms, all of which are epimorphisms. This is the start of an axiomatization of the 'structure at infinity' of the Teichmüller tower as a diagram of groupoid extensions indexed by stable graphs.
errors: Line 3 writes (SΠM_G, Γ') without the subscript A; it should be (S_AΠM_G, Γ'). This is a notational slip.
Equation number (118) is used twice: once in the crossed-out passage and once for the generalization map. The label written over (117) was apparently altered.

The square (119) presupposes that the map S_A → S_{A'} sends the kernel Z^A to Z^{A'} by the projection along C. This is geometrically correct (twists around contracted nodes become trivial loops in M_{G'}). The base-point/tangential-path conventions needed to make the map canonical rather than defined up to conjugacy are left implicit ('expliciter un peu...').

missed.claim: Grothendieck organizes the homotopy type at infinity of M_{g,ν} as a functor from the category of stable graphs (all morphisms epimorphic) to groupoid extensions by Z^{edges}. This is essentially a combinatorial presentation of the stratified homotopy type (exit-path category) of the DM stack, or equivalently of the Kato–Nakayama space. Both of these were formalized later and independently. The link is natural, and the log/combinatorial-anabelian literature (Mochizuki, Hoshi) has largely realized it, so novelty is modest.

missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is a historical precursor for treating \bar M_{g,n} via graph-indexed diagrams of groupoids, relevant to the Grothendieck–Teichmüller action on the tower. The full axiomatization is unfinished on these pages and could be compared with existing modular-operad / exit-path formulations.

deep.surprise_reason: The content is the natural construction of boundary inertia extensions and their compatibility under edge contraction. It is careful and anticipates the later Teichmüller-tower and log-fundamental-groupoid formalisms, but those exist in the literature. There is no finished result here that is absent from it.
transcription_corrections: Line 3: '(SΠM_G, Γ')' is in the manuscript, but presumably S_AΠM_G is meant.
The two vertical arrows in the square are unlabelled; Γ_{G,G'} is written above the top horizontal arrow (≃?), not as an arrow label of a quotient.
The handwritten correction near 'G'' reads 'G' ≃ G/C est une généralisation de G' (the word 'applicat[ion]' is struck out), rather than 'quotient [?]'.
The final line reads 'compatible avec l'action de Γ_{G,G'}, dans la deuxième flèche horizontale ; si on tient...' — continued on the next page.
